newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam coffee prices stable ahead of new crop.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam coffee prices stable ahead of new crop.

text.p: Vietnam robusta coffee prices have remained generally stable in very quiet trading ahead of the arrival of the new harvest, dealers said on Friday.
They said robusta had been trading at between $1,200 and $1,260 per tonne FOB Saigon Port this week against prices of up to $1,290 a week earlier.
"We've had beans starting to come in from Dong Nai province over the last couple of days, but it's difficult to say when we'll see the first of the new harvest from Daklak," one trader said.
Others said that because of recent rains they did not expect to see shipments from the new harvest before November.
Vietnam's coffee season runs from October to September each year and Daklak is the main producing region.
Estimates for total coffee exports during the 1995/6 year have varied from 200-230,000 tonnes, but one dealer said he expected at least 280,000 tonnes to be exported from the new 96/97 harvest.
